html:
A magnitude 7.9 earthquake that struck Wenchuan county in Sichuan, western China, on the afternoon of 12 May 2008. About 69,000 people died, about 18,000 more were missing, and millions lost their homes.

Thousands of the dead were children, crushed when their schools collapsed while buildings nearby stood. Parents blamed corrupt officials and builders for "tofu-dreg" schools. The artist Ai Weiwei gathered the names of the dead students and was beaten and harassed for it.

The response was the largest rescue effort in the history of the People's Republic, with troops and many volunteers, and news coverage that was unusually open at first. It came three months before the Beijing Olympics. Compare the Tangshan earthquake of 1976 and the Yushu earthquake two years later on the Tibetan plateau.
